## Status

## 1. Scope

Covers WP1 sample tracking from field collection at Pallasjärvi through extraction, sequencing, and analysis-ready metadata — designed to stay compatible with WP2 (Grimsö) metadata so the two work packages can eventually be merged for cross-site comparison.

::: {.callout-note}

Now that Pallasjärvi is prospective (not archived) and the Swedish national archive samples are out of scope, WP1 is effectively single-site. Worth stating that explicitly here so anyone picking up this document later understands why the design changed from the original proposal.

:::

## 2. Connectivity definition (operational)

Since there's no multi-year history to select connected/unconnected dyads from, connectivity for WP1 must be defined from within-campaign data:

::: {.callout-important}

**PLACEHOLDER** — exact operational definition, e.g. co-capture at the same trap station/burrow within the 3–4 night session vs. capture on distant grids. This determines what counts as a "connected" vs. "unconnected" dyad
in the eventual model, and should be pinned down before the pilot (it affects what metadata absolutely must be captured in the field — see §4).

:::

## 4. Metadata schema

Minimum fields to capture per sample, matching §4 of the fieldwork protocol:

| Field | Description | Captured by |
|---|---|---|
| sample_id | Unique ID per §3 | Field team |
| grid_id | Trapping grid identifier | Field team |
| trap_station_id | Trap location within grid | Field team |
| gps_lat / gps_lon | Coordinates | Field team |
| capture_date | Date of capture | Field team |
| trap_night | Which night of the 3–4 night session (1–4) | Field team |
| individual_id | Unique animal identifier | Field team |
| species | | Field team |
| sex / age_class / mass | If routinely recorded | Field team |
| burrow_id | If a burrow was associated with this capture | Field team |
| trap_to_burrow_distance_m | | Field team |
| sample_types_collected | Which of gut/nest/soil/blood obtained | Field team |
| storage_medium | Frozen / ethanol / preservation buffer | Field team |
| extraction_batch_id | | Lab |
| extraction_date | | Lab |
| extraction_kit_lot | | Lab |
| pcr_batch_id | | Lab |
| sequencing_run_id | | Lab / NGI |

::: {.callout-note}

**PLACEHOLDER** — confirm which fields Heikki's team can realistically capture given field conditions vs. which need to be reconstructed later (e.g., precise GPS per burrow may need a field-friendly method — handheld GPS unit vs. relative distance/bearing from a mapped trap station).

:::

## 5. Batch design

To avoid confounding batch effects with the biological variable of interest:

- Extraction and library-prep batches should be **blocked across grids**, not run grid-by-grid in sequence
- Once the connectivity definition (§2) is settled, batches should also be blocked across connectivity status, so "connected" and "unconnected" individuals aren't systematically processed in different runs
- Field blanks and off-grid soil controls should appear in every batch, not be run separately at the end

::: {.callout-note}

**PLACEHOLDER** — actual randomization scheme once N and grid count are known; a simple stratified-random assignment to batches is probably sufficient, but worth deciding the block size against expected batch capacity (how many
samples per extraction/PCR run).

:::
